Definition:
When you cast a spell that involves a weapon attack or spell attack, you gain a +2 bonus to those attack rolls.

**Lesser Advancement**
You gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls on attacks that qualify for the bonus above.

**Greater Advancement**
When you make an attack or spell attack that qualifies for the effects above and roll a result of 1 or 2 on the d20, you can reroll the d20 and keep the new result.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

**Lesser Advancement**
Your ranged weapon damage rolls gain a +2 bonus.

**Greater Advancement**
Once per turn, you can ignore all except total cover on an attack with a ranged weapon and gain advantage on that attack.

You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric spell list. They count as belonging to the spell list of the class that allowed you to take this Fighting Style (even if that class has no Spellcasting feature). You use Charisma as your spellcasting ability for these cantrips and any other spells gained through this Fighting Style. Whenever you gain a level you can replace one of these cantrips with another from the Cleric spell list.

**Lesser Advancement**
Choose one additional cantrip from the Cleric spell list. You add your spellcasting ability modifier to the damage dealt by all cantrips you gain(ed) through this Fighting Style.

**Greater Advancement**
Choose one 1st-level spell from the Cleric or Paladin spell list. You can cast this spell a number of times per Long Rest equal to your proficiency bonus, requiring no spell slot or material components. You can also cast this spell using appropriate spell slots.

You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn’t behind total cover, even if you’re blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see invisible creatures within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

**Lesser Advancement**
Your blindsight increases to 30 feet.

**Greater Advancement**
Your blindsight increases to 10 feet x your proficiency bonus.

While you are wearing armor you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

**Lesser Advancement**
The AC bonus increases to +2.

**Greater Advancement**
While you are wearing armor, all piercing, slashing, and bludgeoning damage you receive is reduced by your proficiency bonus.

When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

**Lesser Advancement**
When you roll a 1 or a 2 on an attack roll made using a weapon that qualifies for this style’s extra damage, you can reroll the d20 and keep the new result.

**Greater Advancement**
The +2 bonus to damage rolls becomes equal to your proficiency bonus instead.

When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

**Lesser Advancement**
Your damage rolls with two-handed or versatile weapons gain a +2 bonus.

**Greater Advancement**
You reroll damage dice as described above on a result of 1, 2, or 3, and take the result only if it is higher.

If you did not already have it you gain proficiency with simple firearms. You gain a +2 bonus with attack rolls with firearms, and a +2 bonus to the trigger damage rolls made for trigger weapons.

**Lesser Advancement**
If you did not have it, you gain proficiency with martial firearms. When you hit a creature with a trigger weapon you can fire it once as a free action. Reloading trigger weapons only requires a bonus action.

**Greater Advancement**
You are considered to have proficiency with any firearm that has the advanced property as long as you’ve spent at least 10 minutes inspecting it. You can treat weapons with the full reload property as having the heavy reload property instead, and weapons with the heavy reload property as having the reload property instead.

When a creature you can see hits a target (other than you) within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage the target takes by 1d10 + your proficiency bonus to a minimum of 0 damage. You must be wielding a shield or a simple or martial weapon to use this reaction.

**Lesser Advancement**
If Interception reduces the damage to 0, you can make a single attack against the attacker as long as they are within your weapon’s range.

**Greater Advancement**
If the damage is not reduced to 0 you can choose to redirect the remaining damage to yourself, but only taking half of what remains (rounded down).

When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.

**Lesser Advancement**
You can choose to redirect the triggering attack to yourself.

**Greater Advancement**
If the triggering attack hits, it deals half damage to its target.
Stowing and drawing another weapon you are carrying can be done as a free action, no longer requiring an interaction.

When you make the first attack on your turn you can choose to fight with disregard for your personal safety, granting you advantage on attack rolls you make until the end of your turn or until one hits. Consequently, all attack rolls made against you until the start of your next turn have advantage until one hits you.

**Lesser Advancement**
When this feature is used you have advantage on all weapon attacks you make until the start of your next turn.

**Greater Advancement**
Attacks made with advantage through this feature cannot suffer from disadvantage.

You learn one maneuver of your choice from among those available to the Battle Master archetype. If a maneuver you use requires your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver’s effects, the saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

You gain one superiority die, which is a d6 (this die is added to any superiority die you have from another source). This die is used to fuel your maneuvers and is expended when you use it. You regain the expended superiority die when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

**Lesser Advancement**
You gain a second superiority die and learn one more maneuver as described.

**Greater Advancement**
You gain a third superiority die and learn one more maneuver as described.

You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.

In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll.

**Lesser Advancement**
When you roll a 1 or 2 on an attack roll made using a weapon that qualifies for this style’s extra damage, you can reroll the d20 and keep the new result.

**Greater Advancement**
The +2 bonus to damage rolls becomes equal to your proficiency bonus instead.

When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

**Lesser Advancement**
Attack rolls made using your off-hand weapon gain a +2 bonus.

**Greater Advancement**
Attacks made using your off-hand weapon have advantage if your primary weapon attack that preceded it missed.

Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren’t wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8.

At the start of each of your turns you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you.

**Lesser Advancement**
Your unarmed strikes count as weapons with the finesse property, allowing you to enchant them as if they were weapons.

**Greater Advancement**
Your unarmed strikes deal 1d8 damage + your Strength modifier on a hit, or a d10 if you aren’t wielding any weapons or a shield. Your unarmed strikes gain a +2 bonus to their attack rolls.

The proficiency fighting style varies depending on its source. Previous iterations of the fighting style are described in Lyre’s Guide to Retia. If the source of the fighting style does not describe what it gives proficiency in, then choose from the following properties, and the style applies to any weapons with those properties:

• Ammunition
• Cleaving*
• Finesse
• Heavy
• Knuckles*
• Light
• Range
• Reach
• Secondary*
• Thrown
• Versatile

*These properties are described for weapons in Lyre’s Guide to Retia.

You may take the Proficiency fighting style multiple times as long as it’s for different properties/weapons, but if two or more instances of it would overlap with the same weapon you are using, their effects do not stack, and you instead use the most advanced version among them.

**Base**
When you are wielding a weapon that qualifies, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls made with it.

**Lesser Advancement**
When you roll a 1 or a 2 on an attack roll made using a weapon that qualifies for this Style’s extra damage, you can reroll the d20 and must keep the new result.

**Greater Advancement**
The +2 bonus to damage rolls becomes equal to your proficiency bonus instead.
